slides.title: In 1919 a wave of molasses up to 25 feet high hit Boston.
15 January 1919
slides.body: A steel tank about 50 feet tall in Boston's North End split open, releasing some 2.3 million gallons of molasses.

slides.title: About 35 miles per hour
slides.body: The wave, estimated at up to 25 feet high, crushed buildings and buckled an elevated railway. 21 people died and about 150 were injured.

slides.title: It got thicker
slides.body: A 2016 study found the molasses thickened fast in the cold air, trapping victims and slowing rescue.

slides.title: Painted to hide the leaks
slides.body: The tank had leaked since its first filling in 1915. It was painted brown to hide the seepage, and it had never been properly tested.

slides.title: The company blamed anarchists
slides.body: A court-appointed auditor found it responsible after three years of hearings. It paid about $628,000, and Massachusetts tightened its building rules.

caption: A tank that leaked from day one, painted brown so the seepage wouldn't show, and a wave of molasses up to 25 feet high. Which detail is the worst?
